parts.note: a sudden fit of frenzied excitement, whose name, lacking only its opening letter, is a downpour with wind, so the word is almost wholly a wet spell

explanation.surface: Someone's emotional explosion leaves them nearly drenched in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two words define a sudden mental frenzy; the rest is a play on the spelling, since dropping the first letter leaves RAINSTORM, so the word is almost entirely a wet one.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainstorm in the older sense is a sudden violent fit of emotion or mental disturbance, a passionate outburst.

parts.note: musicians on a spring bloom, but the ship is meant and the group is its travelling settlers

explanation.surface: Performers stand on a spring blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mayflower carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620; a band is also a group of travellers, while 'Entertainers' suggests musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A company of pilgrims is the group who sailed on the Mayflower; a band is both musicians and a party of people.

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters take on an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A plant in the Pyrenean principality is so unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges ANDORRA SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron's rod is a name for great mullein and other tall flowering plants.

clue.text: She comes from the Orient in a pleasant dress

indicators.note: to dress something is to clothe it, so the pleasant word wraps round the letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A woman arrives from the East wearing an attractive frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' is a verb: NICE clothes E (the East).
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a female relative, so a woman stands for her.

indicators.note: trick suggests the cards are shuffled by sleight of hand, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A conjuror's card trick is attributed to a Victorian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trick' rearranges TEN CARD; Benjamin Disraeli, the Victorian prime minister, also wrote novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Tancred is the hero and title of an 1847 novel by Disraeli.

clue.text: Hit with everyone round the Italian resort

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
all means everyone
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A punch-up involving the whole crowd breaks out at a seaside town in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapallo is a resort town on the Ligurian coast of Italy.

parts.note: Burke's partner in the notorious body-snatching pair, and also a pacemaker who leads a race from the front

explanation.surface: A question about who led the field for someone called Burke.
explanation.walkthrough: Burke and Hare were 1820s Edinburgh murderers who sold corpses for dissection; separately, a hare is the pacemaker in a race or the quarry in a paper chase.
explanation.definitionFit: The partner of William Burke, and an animal or runner that sets the pace at the front.

clue.text: A levy on a coral island

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A tax is imposed on a tropical reef island.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped reef of coral enclosing a lagoon.

indicators.note: about here means turned around, the letters moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about drowsy tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SLEEPY AIRS; 'Complaint' means an illness, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Erysipelas is a bacterial skin infection, an ailment or medical complaint.

definitions.meaning: the honour of making the most runs in an innings
printed as one run, read as 'over twenty': top means over and a score is twenty

explanation.surface: A cricketer gets an honour for passing twenty runs.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'over' and 'twenty' together; read apart, TOP (over) and SCORE (twenty) give the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest innings in a match is a batsman's honour, and over a score is literally top plus twenty.

definitions.meaning: to tend or look after someone who is ill
the ... hound, a large spotted dogfish

explanation.definitionFit: To tend the sick is to nurse them, and the nurse hound or nurse shark is a kind of dogfish.

clue.text: Suitable subject for one with his head in the clouds

definitions.text: Suitable subject for one with his head in the clouds

parts.words: Suitable subject for one with his head in the clouds
parts.note: the idiom for a dreamer is read literally: the field of study that deals with clouds

explanation.surface: A daydreamer is advised which course to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head in the clouds' usually means absent-minded; here it is taken literally, pointing to the science of clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephology is the branch of meteorology that studies clouds.

indicators.note: the letters of the shape's name are put into a new form, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson calls a three-sided figure fundamental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' makes the anagram of TRIANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral means essential or fundamental, part of the basic whole.

indicators.note: the letters of the religion's name are spread about and dealt out afresh

explanation.surface: Meals are handed out within a Muslim community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges ISLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a ragout of game birds, a dish of food.

parts.note: 'for aye' is an old phrase meaning for ever

explanation.surface: Something was under assault for an eternity and one more day.
explanation.walkthrough: The old phrase FOR AYE means 'for ever'; add D for day.
explanation.definitionFit: To foray is to make a raid, so forayed means made a raiding attack.

clue.text: Some potty earl in gambling row over young horse

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mad aristocrat's betting causes a quarrel over a foal.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'row over young horse' as the definition, but only 'young horse' defines; 'row over' is surface padding linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, between one and two years old.

parts.note: ob., short for Latin obiit 'died', marks a person of the past
an ovate is a learned member of the Welsh bardic order, ranking between druid and bard

explanation.surface: A former student is called an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like a brainy person, but it means a shape like an egg with its broad end at the head; an ovate is a rank in the Welsh Gorsedd of bards.
explanation.definitionFit: Obovate describes a leaf egg-shaped with the broader end at the top, like an egg standing on its narrow end.

clue.text: Forbearing to be drunk at best inn

indicators.note: being drunk suggests the letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resists the temptation of getting drunk at the finest pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be drunk' rearranges AT BEST INN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinent means refraining from indulgence, especially from drink, so self-restraining.

clue.text: State of a third man in the subcontinent

parts.note: the Indian subcontinent is chiefly the country of India

indicators.note: third picks out the letter in third place in the word man

explanation.surface: A question about the condition of a third person living in South Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third' takes the third letter of 'man', N; with A, that follows INDIA, the subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a state of the American Midwest.

clue.text: Biblical city opposed to a Scots expression

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to
och is a Scottish exclamation

explanation.surface: A Scotsman exclaims his dislike of an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch in Syria appears in the Acts of the Apostles as an early Christian centre.

parts.note: to liberate is to set free
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sets a person free while carrying a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant South African plant grown for its blooms.

clue.text: May do the trick if sense is applied

indicators.note: the letters are worked over and put to use in a different order

explanation.surface: Good sense, used well, might be the solution to a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is applied' rearranges IF SENSE; 'trick' is a trick at bridge or whist, won by a finesse.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a finesse is a play that may win a trick with a lower card.

clue.text: Give the third degree to cook

definitions.meaning: to cook food under direct heat

explanation.definitionFit: To grill is both to interrogate intensely and to cook under a hot element.

clue.text: A place by the fireside in Gleneagles

annotationWithheld.why: A place by the fireside in Gleneagles (5): INGLE is hidden in 'in Gleneagles', so 'in' must be both the hidden-word indicator and part of the hidden letters; no other word signals the hiding
annotationWithheld.clue: A place by the fireside in Gleneagles

parts.note: the television set is 'the box'; adjusting it to a channel is the phrase meant

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with a container to fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is slang for television; adjusting a set to receive a station is the act described.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuning in means adjusting a radio or television set to pick up a station or programme.

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: A seer who might be a mortal person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges HUMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is a minor prophet of the Old Testament with a book under his name.

clue.text: Worldly as one becomes in colour

indicators.note: one letter becomes part of the colour word by going in it

parts.note: lac is a red resin used as a dye or colour
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person turns worldly as they take on colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes in' puts I inside LAC, the resinous dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay or secular, not of the clergy, so worldly.

parts.note: in means fashionable or with-it

indicators.note: sounds says the word for a prodigy is heard here as the closing part of another word

parts.note: a prodigy is a genius

explanation.surface: Someone is told how skilful the trendy wonder-child sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: IN (with-it) then GENIUS (prodigy), which, spoken, gives the ending of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenious means clever and inventive, showing masterly skill.

parts.note: reads as a person caught giggling, but means an animal species called both spotted and laughing

explanation.surface: Someone was noticed in the middle of a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'noticed', but describes the coat of the African scavenger also known as the laughing one.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena of Africa is also called the laughing hyena for its cackling call.

clue.text: Where a top Olympian stages a come-back

indicators.note: coming back means the god's name is read in the other direction

parts.note: Zeus was king of the gods on Mount Olympus

explanation.surface: A leading athlete from the Games makes a return to competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests an athlete but means the chief Greek god; 'stages a come-back' turns ZEUS round.
explanation.definitionFit: The defining word stands for a place, here the Egyptian canal town and isthmus.

indicators.note: out says the letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A large group of campers has its tents struck, and nobody minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges L (fifty) with EIGHT and CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmatic person is calm and unexcitable, untroubled by events.
